title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
New Jersey fined DataOne $1.07 million after state inspectors found 62 natural gas generators at a data center construction site in Vineland in late July. The 2,000 kilowatt generators, each about the size of a tractor trailer, lacked required permits to be installed or operated. Officials said the penalty for violating the state's Air Pollution Control Act was the largest ever issued to a data center operator in New Jersey. The fine was announced Tuesday.

The Vineland campus is planned as a complex of 2.6 million square feet needing 350 megawatts, enough to power a city of medium size, and is slated for completion at the end of the year. Some of it is already in use. It has drawn complaints, including a federal lawsuit by homeowners over persistent noise and violation orders from the Cumberland County Health Department for excessive noise. Governor Mikie Sherrill said at a Climate Week event that data center development must benefit New Jersey communities.
